text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonian decathlon athlete Erkki Nool failed in the long jump and has no hope of winning a medal at Athens.
- The government set up a commission to deal with Estonian cultural property abroad.
- The director of the Security Police Juri Pihl confirmed the newspaper's reports that the Estonian authorities bought 500 register cards of KGB agents in 1992.
- The rescue service will receive its first modern helicopter with special search equipment at the end of August.
- The police confiscated 3000 pirate CD-s in a raid on kiosks at the Kadaka market in Tallinn last week.
- 180 large families will receive 500 kroons each at the beginning of the new school-year from a special fund formed by Krediidipank, the board of the fund decided yesterday.
- Hansapank decided to provide 500,000 kroon support to the Keila SOS-children's village, chairman Hannes Tamjarv said.
- Serious problems may accompany rapid economic growth in Estonia, an analyst at Price Waterhouse, Hardo Pajula, said.
- Tallinn Transport Department plans to raise ticket prices for public transport from four to five kroons in September, head of the department Tiit Kivikas said.
- Fuel firms in Estonia have began merger talks. The companies Favora and Petra are expected to be the first.
- The tax police in St.Petersburg have blocked the accounts of seven Estonian commercial banks with a total of half a billion kroons and is demanding the payments of taxes.
